title: 第二章 共和国中的皇帝

zh: 现代关于拜占庭政治意识形态的研究在很大程度上忽略了

的核心地位，而后文各章将表明，我们因此也忽略了它对拜占庭政治实际运作方式的意涵。这一失误的主要后果是，我们对拜占庭意识形态与政治的理解狭隘地聚焦于皇帝，仿佛他是唯一相关的政治场域。我们为政治领域构建的本体论由一个超自然实体上帝、一个历史性的政治行动者皇帝及其治理工具（“国家”）、以及一大群“臣民”构成，而这些臣民似乎除了由其宗教和身为皇帝臣民这一事实所赋予的身份外别无身份。这一错误的根源最终在于我们拒绝认真对待他们的罗马身份。正因如此，在主导图式中，他们是相对于皇帝被定义的，而不是像拜占庭人所见的那样，皇帝相对于他们被定义。在我们眼中他们没有政治身份，因而既没有也不构成一个真正的
。重申本书的论点：拜占庭的罗马身份不仅是宣示性的，而且嵌入政治领域的构造之中。当我们把其中之一弄错时，就不可避免地也会误解另一个。
en: Modern scholarship on Byzantine political ideology has largely missed the centrality of the

and later chapters will reveal that we have accordingly missed its implications for how politics were actually conducted in Byzantium. The chief result of this failure is that our understanding of Byzantine ideology and politics is narrowly focused on the emperor as if he were the only relevant political site. The ontology that we have constructed for the political sphere consists of a supernatural entity, God; a historical political agent, the emperor, and his instruments of governance (“the state”); and a mass of “subjects” who seem to have had no identity other than that conferred on them by their religion and the fact that they were subjects of the emperor. The root of this error lies ultimately in our refusal to take their Roman identity seriously. That is why, in the dominant schema, they are defined in relation to the emperor and not, as the Byzantines saw it, the emperor in relation to them. Having no political identity in our eyes, they neither have nor constitute a true

To repeat the thesis of this book, Roman identity in Byzantium was not merely assertive but embedded in the configuration of the political sphere. When we get one of them wrong, we invitably misunderstand the other too.

zh: 现代对拜占庭政治领域的重构只关注其两种赋予合法性的意识形态之一，即神权式的那种，而排斥共和式的那种。这两者共存，尽管运作于不同层面与不同语境，这一问题我们将在第6章讨论。我们对神权模式的固着使我们把权威的流向理解成单纯自上而下的过程。但共和模式授权一种自下而上的视角，据此皇帝从罗马人民那里获得权威，并在理论与事实上都对他们负责。若我们忽略共和国即
，这一视角对我们就是关闭的。共和国在时间上先于君主制，而我主张它在帝国之下也仍在理论上先于君主制：
是依照
被定义和证成的，而非相反。政体并非自主，因为它严格说来并非自成法律，正如我们在阅读利奥的
时所见。
是政权合法性的来源，但它需要那个政权——无论是君主制还是罗马共和国时期的制度——以政权为中介，向这个共同体自身表明其正当性。罗马政体不是一种特定类型的政权，而是一个持有平民主义意识形态的人民的政治领域。我们的学术迄今未承认它的存在，尽管它在拜占庭史料中无处不在（话说回来，罗马之名也是如此，而现代史家一直刻意回避它）。
en: Modern reconstructions of the Byzantine political sphere focus on only one of its two legitimizing ideologies, the theocratic one, and excludes the republican. These two coexisted although they operated on different levels and in different contexts, an issue we will discuss in Chapter 6. Our fixation on the theocratic model has drawn lines of authority in an exclusively top-down way. But the republican model authorizes a bottom-up perspective according to which the emperor derived his authority from the Roman people and was answerable to them in both theory and fact. This perspective is barred to us if we overlook the republic, or
The republic was chronologically prior to the monarchy, and I propose that it also remained theoretically prior to the monarchy under the empire: it was in terms of the
that the
was defined and justified, not the reverse. The polity was not autonomous because it was not strictly speaking a law unto itself, as we saw in our reading of Leon’s
The

was the source of the regime’s legitimacy, but it needed that regime, whether a monarchy or Republic, to represent its own legitimacy to itself. The Roman polity was not a specific type of regime but the political sphere of a people with a populist ideology. Our scholarship has not so far recognized its existence, even though it is pervasive in the Byzantine sources (then again, so is the Roman name, which modern historians have scrupulously avoided).

zh: 拜占庭的“共和国”与“国家”
en: “Republic” and “State” in Byzantium

zh: 部分问题在于现代术语“国家”干扰了我们看见罗马人
的能力。我们的“国家”一词依照与罗马共和传统不同的标准与区分来组织权力关系。关于该词是否甚至适用于前现代语境也存在分歧。让-克洛德·谢内（Jean-Claude Cheynet）论拜占庭写道：“国家的观念，作为罗马世界的遗产，过分集中体现于皇帝一身，因而不能独立发挥作用……在这一时期，它已在很大程度上让位于个人纽带。”
依此立场，
罗马人既有国家也有国家概念（尽管谢内未告诉我们那概念是什么），但拜占庭人虽继承了该概念，实践中却只有皇帝。然而我们必须小心“国家观念”与“罗马世界遗产”所指为何。例如 Jon Lendon 论证道，古代罗马人同样“不把自己的帝国看作一个抽象物。对皇帝的臣民而言，所有统治者加在一起是‘当局’而非‘国家’。”
我理解他的意思是他们也没有“国家概念”。于是依我们所追随的人不同，罗马人和拜占庭人都没有国家概念，而只以掌握权力的个人来思考。在拜占庭的情形中，这些人便是皇帝及其职能官员。
en: Part of the problem is that the modern term “state” has interfered with our ability to see the Romans’

Our term “state” organizes relations of power along different criteria and distinctions than does the Roman republican tradition. There is also disagreement about whether the term is even applicable in premodern contexts. Jean-Claude Cheynet has written about Byzantium that “the idea of a state, a heritage of the Roman world, was too incarnated in the emperor to be in itself efficacious... In this period, it had largely given place to personal ties.”
According to this position, the

Romans had both a state and the concept of a state (though Cheynet does not tell us what that concept was), but the Byzantines, while inheriting that concept, had only an emperor in practice. We have to be careful, however, about what we mean by “the idea of the state” and “the heritage of the Roman world.” Jon Lendon, for example, has argued that the ancient Romans too “did not see their empire as an abstraction. To the emperor’s subjects all their rulers together were ‘the authorities’ rather than ‘the state.’ ”

I take it he means that they had no “concept of the state” either. So depending on whom we follow, neither the Romans nor the Byzantines had a concept of the state and thought merely in terms of individuals who held power. In the Byzantine case these would have been the emperor and his functionaries.

zh: 诚然，个人纽带很重要，权力关系常以个人道德语汇来表象。但这与非人格的国家并不矛盾。我生活过的两个国家——美国与希腊——都在某种程度上由代代传递权力的政治家族治理。华盛顿充斥着任人唯亲与裙带关系，而在希腊，非人格的
被许多人用作交换个人恩惠的门面。但这并不意味着那个观念不存在。事实上，非人格的国家在意识形态上占主导，并解释了民众对这些现象的不满。不存在个人权力的
；它无法在公共场合被辩护甚至被表述。因此我抵制这样一种看法：凡我们能检测到个人网络运作之处，就不可能存在非人格的国家。
所以，尽管个人关系对国家机器与社会的
运作极为重要，这些关系的总和并不等于国家这一现象。
en: To be sure, personal ties were important and relations of power were often represented in personal moral terms. But this is not incompatible with the impersonal state. Both of the countries in which I have lived, the United States and Greece, are governed in part by political dynasties that pass power from generation to generation in a hereditary way. Washington is rife with cronyism and nepotism, while in Greece the impersonal

is exploited by many as a façade for the exchange of personal favors. But that does not mean that the idea is not there. In fact, the impersonal state is ideologically dominant and explains the disaffection of the populace at these phenomena. There is no

of personal power; it cannot be defended or even articulated in public. Therefore, I resist the idea that an impersonal state cannot have existed wherever we can detect the operation of personal networks.
So while personal relationships were hugely important for the functioning of the state apparatus and society
the totality of those relations does not amount to the phenomenon of the state.

zh: 拜占庭亦然。虽然可以像谢内那样说拜占庭国家实际上只是一张发自皇帝的个人关系之网，但要把这一观点一贯地应用于它实际如何运作的分析却是不可能的。例如 Haldon 与 Brubaker 新近写道：“拜占庭官僚体系不是一个匿名、独立、自我调节的行政结构……[而是]一个以同心圆一层层展开、由庇护者和依附者结成的家产制网络，集中于宫廷周围，更重要的是集中于皇帝个人周围。”
但不仅他们的书主要讲的是机构在人事变动中的延续，而且当他们总结其关于它如何运作的结论时，我们看到的恰是相反的图景，而我认为那更正确。
en: The same was true of Byzantium. While it is possible to say, as Cheynet did, that the Byzantine state was in reality only a web of personal relations that emanated from the emperor, it is impossible to apply that view consistently in an analysis of how it actually functioned. For example, Haldon and Brubaker have recently written that “the Byzantine bureaucratic system was not an anonymous, independent, and self-regulating administrative structure... [but] a patrimonial network of concentric circles of clientage and patronage, concentrated around the imperial court and, more importantly, around the person of the emperors.”

But not only is their book largely about the continuity of institutions despite changes in personnel, when they summarize their conclusions about how it worked, we find the exact opposite picture, which I think is more correct.

zh: 政府与宫廷，尽管政治权力常在不同统治者及拥护他们的派系和利益集团之间发生戏剧性转移，却保持稳定并继续运作……常备军通过一个资源独立于皇室之外的行政机器得以维持……即便在最严重的危机中[皇帝阵亡时]国家也几乎未被动摇……国家的财政与行政机器几乎在一片安宁中继续运转……这种制度稳定根深蒂固，国家及其机器嵌入社会—政治秩序之中。
en: The government and court, in spite of often dramatic transfers of political power from ruler to ruler and their supporting factions and vested interests, remained stable and continued to function... A standing army was maintained through an administrative apparatus whose resources were independent of the imperial household... Even in the worst of crises [when an emperor was killed in battle] the state was hardly shaken... The state’s fiscal and administrative machinery was kept running with barely a murmur of unease... Institutional stability of this sort was deeply rooted, and the state and its apparatus were embedded in the social-political order.

zh: 正如一位现代理论家所指出的，“制度稳定的本质在于把首要忠诚从皇帝转移到一个抽象化的国家观念上。”
拜占庭确有制度稳定，而我们将看到，拜占庭人也有一种抽象的政治共同体观念，主要指罗马人的共和国。
en: As a modern theorist has noted, “the essence of institutional stability was the transfer of primary allegiance away from the emperor and toward an abstracted conception of the state.”
Byzantium certainly had institutional stability, and we will see that it too had an abstracted sense not so much of a state as of a republic, the republic of the Romans.

zh: Cheynet、Lendon 与 Haldon 关于拜占庭人
的所有否定性论证都以有问题的语汇框定。首先，他们未能讨论甚至识别罗马人的
观念，无论在早期帝国还是拜占庭语境中。Fergus Millar 正确地指出，若要评估罗马人（或其继承者）是否持有非人格观念，我们必须聚焦

谢内未说明他所认为的“罗马世界遗产”是什么，Lendon 也未解释为何聚焦“帝国”概念而非

，无论帝国时期的罗马人自己怎么想。“帝国”是含混的。Lendon 指的恐怕不是罗马人对非罗马人的统治权。依照惯例，他用“帝国”指“奥古斯都之后的罗马国家”，从而把国家与皇帝混同，并遮蔽了这样一个事实：
的基本原则仍在延续，并且随着希腊人也逐渐变成罗马人，甚至殖民了希腊语词
的语义范围。换言之，若对帝国时期罗马人持有非人格“国家”的否认是建立在对他们理解自身政治领域与公共利益之术语的彻底考察之上，那会更令人安心。但这些情形中并未进行这样的考察。
en: All the negative arguments by Cheynet, Lendon, and Haldon about what the Byzantines
are framed in problematic terms. First, they fail to discuss or even identify the Roman idea of the
whether in the early imperial or Byzantine context. Fergus Millar has correctly observed that we have to focus on the idea of the
if we are to assess whether the Romans (or their heirs) had an impersonal concept: “the notion of a state as a
an impersonal entity logically distinct from the individuals exercising power, was an important legacy of Roman law.”
Cheynet does not specify what he takes “the heritage of the Roman world” to have been, and Lendon does not explain why he focuses on the concept of “empire” rather than the
His choice seems to reflect the modern Republican bias according to which there was no

after Augustus, regardless of what the Romans of the empire may have thought. “Empire” is ambiguous. It is doubtful that Lendon is referring to the dominion that Romans held over non-Romans. Following convention, he uses “empire” to refer to “the Roman state after Augustus,” thereby conflating the state with the emperor and occluding the fact that the basic principles of the

Put differently, it would have been more reassuring if the denial that the Romans of the empire had an impersonal “state” was based on a thorough examination of the terms by which they understood their own political sphere and the public interest. But no such examination has been undertaken in these cases.

zh: 在否认非人格罗马国家的存在时，谢内以及可能 Lendon 是在呼应现代理论家中相当确立的观点，即非人格国家出现于近代早期，而在此之前“公共权力是以远为个人化和卡里斯玛化的语汇被对待的”。

这有时被称为“家产制国家”，即君主的财产。若这一虚构与任何实际的中世纪政体有关系，它与拜占庭也几乎或完全没有关系。此外，并非所有中世纪史家都信服他们不能使用“国家”一词。虽然政治学家中对国家没有普遍公认的定义，一些前现代史家提供了反映该词常规用法的概括定义。例如 Susan Reynolds 把国家定义为“在固定领土内的人类社会组织，它或多或少成功地宣称对该领土内合法使用物理力量的控制（而非垄断）”。她还论证道，“若依此定义以流动性等理由否认中世纪王国或较小领地的国家地位……那就也得否认许多现代国家的国家地位。”
Haldon 在拜占庭学者中是例外，他常在使用国家概念前先定义它。在他看来，国家是一个领土实体，其中央权力垄断对强力的使用；它必须有一套意识形态体系；并必须随时间再生产其功能。
无疑依这些标准拜占庭够格称为国家，无论拜占庭人是否为该概念持有固定术语。拜占庭是一个国家为几乎所有史家所接受，无论出于直觉还是有理论定义支持。谢内是怀疑它的例外，但也许他怀疑的只是拜占庭国家是否完全非人格；也许他只是在强调皇帝作为个人行动者的至上性。
en: In denying the existence of an impersonal Roman state, Cheynet and possibly Lendon are echoing a fairly established view among modern theorists according to which the impersonal state emerged in early modernity, whereas before that “public power had been treated in far more personal and charismatic terms.”

This is sometimes called the “patrimonial state,” which is the property of the monarch. If this fiction bears any relation to actual medieval polities, it has little or none to Byzantium. Moreover, not all medieval historians are persuaded that they cannot use the term “state.” While there is no universally agreed-upon definition of the state among political scientists, some premodern historians offer general definitions that reflect conventional uses of the term. For example, Susan Reynolds defines the state as “an organization of human society within a fixed territory that more or less successfully claims the control (not the monopoly) of the legitimate use of physical force within that territory.” She argues, moreover, that “if one were to deny statehood on this definition to medieval kingdoms or lesser lordships in general... on grounds of fluidity etc. one would have to deny it to a good many modern states.”

Haldon is exceptional among Byzantinists in that he often defines the concept of the state before using it. In his view, a state is a territorial entity with a center that exerts a monopoly on force; it must have an ideological system; and it must reproduce its functions over time.

There is no doubt that in these terms Byzantium qualifies as a state, regardless of whether or not the Byzantines had a fixed term for that concept. That Byzantium was a state is accepted by almost all historians, whether intuitively or backed by theoretical definitions. Cheynet is exceptional in doubting it, but perhaps he is doubting only that the Byzantine state was fully impersonal; perhaps he is only stressing the supremacy of the emperor as a personal agent.

zh: 那么这在理论上把我们置于何地？我们似乎面临两种选择：要么把拜占庭国家看作皇帝个人统治及其与臣民个人关系的产物，从而断定拜占庭人没有“非人格的”国家观（因而根本没有真正的国家）；要么以或多或少现代的语汇设定一个拜占庭国家，它可与治理它的个人以及“其权力所施于的整个社会……既区别于统治者也区别于被统治者”相分离——引用现代国家概念起源理论家昆廷·斯金纳（Quentin Skinner）的话。
我迄今的讨论似乎倾向于非人格国家，与上文长段引用 Haldon 与 Brubaker 一致。但事实上两种选择都不能充分表象罗马的
。个人化定义不反映罗马人或拜占庭人如何思考其政体，后者不能被还原为
，因为
的地位和作用由
所决定。至于完全非人格的定义，虽然它使我们能以可辨识的现代语汇谈论拜占庭国家 （这种分析往往恰当而有用），它却遮蔽了支配该国家运作的共和意识形态。那个政体从它与皇帝的关系来看，不依赖于皇帝个人，因为它意指罗马人民的集体事务。但它不能从他们的整体道德共同体中抽象出来，所以不能说它独立于罗马人民这一方——现代理论会把后者塞进“市民社会”范畴。罗马集体不只是市民社会；它是一个政治共同体。
就是
，“罗马人民的财产与事务”。那么国家与共和国之间是什么关系？
en: So where does this leave us in terms of theory? We seem to face two alternatives: either we view the Byzantine state as an affect of the emperor’s personal rule and of his personal relations with his subjects, thereby concluding that the Byzantines had no “impersonal” view of the state (and so no real state at all), or we postulate a Byzantine state in more or less modern terms as separable from the persons who govern it as well as from “the whole society over which its powers are exercised... distinct from both the rulers are the ruled,” to quote Quentin Skinner, a theorist of the origin of the modern concept of the state.

My discussion so far has seemed to argue in favor of the impersonal state, consistent with the long quotation of Haldon and Brubaker given above. But in fact neither alternative adequately represents the Roman
The personal definition does not reflect how Romans or Byzantines thought of their polity, which could not be reduced to the
as the latter was a function of the

As for a fully impersonal definition, while it enables us to talk about the Byzantine state in recognizably modern terms (an often appropriate and useful exercise), it does obscure the republican ideology that governed the operations of that state. That polity was impersonal when viewed in relation to the emperor, as it signified the collective affairs of the Roman people. But it could not be abstracted from their overall moral community and so was not impersonal when viewed in relation to the Roman people, whom modern theory would box into the category of “civil society.” The Roman collectivity was not just a civil society; it was a political community. The
was the
“the property and business of the Roman people.” What was the relationship, then, between state and republic?

zh: 为更好解释所涉理论区分，我将使用斯金纳关于现代国家概念起源的历史。我在此这样做纯粹为了概念清晰，并不要求他的图式准确描述实地历史进程；我的主要关切是把拜占庭政体相对于政治学所用理论模型加以分类，并用这一政体补充政治学的基本模型。依斯金纳，从中世纪所谓的“个人统治”出发，共和理论家首先把统治机器抽象出来并与统治者个人分离。“他们认为，世俗政府的权力由一套法律和制度体现，统治者与官员受托以共同福祉的名义执行法律并管理这些制度。”但他们未区分

之体（人民）与国家。国家术语“因此被设想为不过是以行政上更便利的形式表达人民权力的一种手段”（而且如我们所见，共和“国家”可以是君主制的）。“人民权力与国家权力之间[未]划出有效对照。”我称之为共和式的国家观念。依斯金纳，只是后来绝对主义理论家——尤其霍布斯——才把国家也从人民及整个市民社会中抽象出来。作为这第二步的结果，“国家在现代想象中倾向于呈现为一个单一、自立的行为体，一个永远被某种不可渗透的膜与它所支配的社会隔开的行为体。”
en: To better explain the theoretical distinctions at stake, I will use Skinner’s history of the origins of the concept of the modern state. I do so here solely for the purposes of conceptual clarity, without requiring that his schema accurately describes historical processes on the ground; my chief concern is to classify the Byzantine polity in relation to the theoretical models used in political science, and also to put it forward as a supplement to their basic repertoire. According to Skinner, then, from the allegedly “personal rule” of the Middle Ages, republican theorists first abstracted the apparatus of rule and separated it from the ruler’s person. “They [thought] of the powers of civil government as embodied in a structure of laws and institutions which our rulers and magistrates are entrusted to administer in the name of the common good.” But they did not distinguish between the body of the

(the people) and the state. Terms for the state were “thus conceived as nothing more than a means of expressing the powers of the people in an administratively more convenient form” (the republican “state,” moreover, could be monarchical, as we saw). “No effective contrast [was] drawn between the power of the people and the powers of the state.” This I will call the republican idea of a state. It was only later, according to Skinner, that absolutist theorists, notably Hobbes, abstracted the state from the people too and from civil society as a whole. As a result of this second move, “the state tends to appear in the modern imagination as a unitary, free-standing agency, one that is forever separated by a kind of impermeable membrane from the society over which it holds sway.”

zh: 这一图式未必是对历史所发生之事的准确描述。国家与社会的分离在现代语境中也可被质疑。
此外，文艺复兴“共和”革命之前的中世纪政体并不像许多现代主义理论家假设的那样“个人化”。我坚持认为拜占庭符合斯金纳的共和国家标准，这并不奇怪，因为它不过是所有早期现代共和理论家所据以建立的古代罗马传统的活态延伸。它作为政治文化的不幸在于，其罗马基础因无关的中世纪论战而在学术中被忽略，这使得皇帝处于真空之中，只由其个人在场填充，或被缠入陈词滥调的神学修辞。若我们重新把
纳入考察，就能看到这个社会的本来面目：一个共和国。
en: This schema is not necessarily an accurate description of what happened historically. The separation of state and society can be doubted in the modern context too.

Moreover, medieval polities prior to the Renaissance “republican” revolution were not as “personal” as many modernist theorists assume. Byzantium, I maintain, meets Skinner’s standards of a republican state, which is not surprising, for it was but a living extension of the ancient Roman tradition on which all early modern republican theorists were building. Its misfortune as a political culture has been that its Roman basis has been overlooked in the scholarship because of irrelevant medieval polemics, which has left the emperor in a vacuum, filled only by his own personal presence or enmeshed in platitudinous theological rhetoric. If we restore the
to the equation, we see this society for what it was: a republic.

zh: 虽然拜占庭确是一个国家并可作为国家来讨论，但对现代理论而言“国家”在很大程度上是从“市民社会”抽象出来并施加于其上的东西。它是一个针对本质上为私人利益场域的调节与保护机构。两者之间由“公共领域”居中联结，它把私人利益与国家利益带入讨论，尽管有些东西（在一端）过于私人而不能进入该领域，另一些东西（在另一端）从国家观点看过于“机密”（因此两者除非被曝光否则都不“公共”）。这一模型在讨论拜占庭时可用到一定程度，但它确实扭曲了
的意识形态。在一个
内部不易把国家与社会其余部分隔离，因为正如我们在第1章通过 Syrianos 所见，
由一切贡献于共同善的东西构成，包括人民与国家机器。人们可以识别在任何时刻或多或少处于皇帝控制之下的治理面向。术语
（权力）与
（皇帝职位或君主制及其权威、职能与延伸）可用来近似我们所谓国家。毕竟

en: While Byzantium certainly was a state and can be discussed as such, “the state” is, for modern theory, something largely abstracted from and imposed upon “civil society.” It is a regulatory and protective agency for what is basically a field of private interests. Mediating between them is the “public sphere,” which brings private and state interests into discussion, though some things are (at the one end) too private to enter that sphere while other things are (at the other end) too “classified” from the state’s point of view (so neither is “public” unless it is exposed). This model may be used up to a point in discussing Byzantium, but it does distort the ideology of the
Within a
one cannot easily isolate the state from the rest of society because, as we saw with Syrianos in Chapter 1, the

is constituted by everything that contributes to the common good, including the people and the apparatus of the state. One could identify the aspects of governance that were more or less under the emperor’s control at any moment. The terms
(power) and
(the imperial office or monarchy and its authority, functions, and extensions) could be used to approximate what we mean by the state. After all, the purpose of the
was to govern and regulate the

But there was no concept of a public sphere to mediate between the state and private interests, for the polity was a political sphere oriented toward the collective good of the Roman people. The emperor’s function was to promote that good. We see here how the modern concept of the state distorts this culture. Not only do the “common-sense” definitions quoted above (by Reynolds and Haldon) fail to mention the common good, they do not say what the state is good for at all. They focus only on its powers. This is a problem of the sociologist’s outside view. As Raymond Geuss has noted, the state thereby becomes “merely an agency operating and exercising powers in a certain way. Part of the object being observed, to be sure, is a set of beliefs about legitimacy held by the members of the state under consideration, but the sociologist may or may not be interested in assessing these beliefs morally.”

虽然这可能是共和国家的一个特征，但它不是其

之一。总之，虽然我们可以说拜占庭是一个国家（或拥有一个国家），现代国家观念无助于我们理解支配拜占庭政体的意识形态。我们需要一种关于皇帝职位的理论，既不同于个人统治（一方面），也不同于自存、惩罚性、非人格的国家（另一方面）。
en: The failure of post-Hobbesian theories of the state to understand republican regimes is most striking in their propensity, in their focus on punitive powers, to define the state in terms of its monopoly of coercive power within a society.
While this may have been a feature of the republican state, it is not a

of it; it is only an attribute. Its definition, for any of its subjects, would have been synonymous with its function, namely, to promote the common good of the Romans. A monopoly on certain kinds of power was only one of the

that enabled it to perform that function. In sum, while we can say that Byzantium was a state (or had one), modern notions of the state do not help us understand the ideology that governed the Byzantine polity. We need a theory for the office of the emperor different both from that of personal rule (on the one hand) and of the selfsubsisting, punitive, and impersonal state (on the other).

As his function was defined by that political community, it was neither personal nor abstracted from it. That polity, moreover, represented a moral consensus, not an abstracted state. Later chapters of this book will fill in other parts of this picture. For now I will focus on the priority of the

en: An episode from the late sixth century illustrates that when emperor and God failed to command respect, the authorities fell back on the soldiers’ devotion to the polity, that is, to their patriotism as Romans, which was also part of their oath. When the eastern armies mutinied in 588 over a pay reduction, the general Priskos tried to cow them by bringing out from Edessa and parading before them the

the holy relic upon which Christ’s image had been impressed, “so that by respect for the holy object, the anger might be humbled.” But the men “pelted the ineffable object with stones” and the general had to run away.

The task fell to Gregorios, the bishop of Antioch, who spoke to them the following year and did appease them. His speech is recorded by his secretary Euagrios, who wrote his history a few years afterward. Gregorios began by addressing the soldiers as “O men, Romans in both name and deed,” and he praised them for defeating the Persians even during their mutiny: “for you have demonstrated that even when you have a grievance toward your generals, there is nothing of greater importance to you than the

en: This speech is revealing, given its circumstances. When “loyalty to the emperor” (the modern misunderstanding of what it meant to be a Roman in Byzantium) and the veneration of relics are stripped away, what was left was the ultimate backbone of Roman patriotism and Byzantine solidarity: devotion to a polity, a

that had endured under both consuls and emperors. Soldiers’ loyalty was to the polity, and Gregorios appealed to their Roman patriotism. The stoning of the relic is also revealing: we will see that when push came to shove, the religious ideology that modern scholarship ascribes to the Byzantines did not count for much.

换言之，不仅皇帝而且其所有官员与士兵，其功能都被相对于政体来理解，其工作表现不断以共同善为标准被评判。这些人不仅服务在位皇帝也服务
，而如我们将见，后者并非空洞观念：这些人常须在两者间抉择，有时致命。Psellos 一生服务多位皇帝，其中一些他并非全心拥戴。但他确常强调自己内心是罗马爱国者。
当政权崩溃、须在皇位竞争者间抉择时，这一品质变得关键。
但即便在稳定时期，Psellos 也知道好政治家须在君主制与政体其余部分之间调解。当他在君士坦丁九世之下拒绝
（首席机要秘书）之职时，普塞洛斯为自己在皇帝身边的作为辩护：“我在许多关乎公共利益（τὰ κοινά）之事上与他合作，向他提出最完善的
，也尽我所见，帮助他尽到一切足以体现君主职责的要求。”
在若干著作中 Psellos 发展了“政治人”理想，后者与其说是完美廷臣，不如说是能在相互竞争的主张之间为全体之善调解的开明公仆。
退休官员约安尼斯·佐纳拉斯认为公共事务处于诸事“之中”。
那个空间不为任何一个人所有。
en: Emperors were not identified with the political sphere, nor were they always personally dominant in it. Others also played a role in determining its fortunes, for good or ill. A corrupt official was “an outrage and disease for the
of the Romans.”
Conversely, the
was something that the imperial officials of all ranks could “do well by” and “endow with something great—or not.”
Mauropous praised an acquaintance as the “shinning eye of the

In other words, it was not only the emperors but all their officials and soldiers whose functions were understood in relation to the polity and whose job performance was continually being judged by the standard of the common good. These people served not only the current emperor but the

too, and, as we will see, the second was not an empty notion: these men often had to choose, sometimes fatally, between the two. Psellos served many emperors in his time, some of them with less than total devotion. He did, however, often stress that he was a Roman patriot at heart.
This quality became critical when a regime was collapsing and choices had to be made between rivals for the throne.
But even in stable times, Psellos knew that a good politician had to mediate between the monarchy and the rest of the polity. When he refused the office of
under Konstantinos IX, Psellos defended his actions at the emperor’s side: “I collaborated with him in many matters regarding the public interest (τὰ κοινά), proposed to him the most perfect
and adapted him to all those things in which monarchy reveals itself, at least as it seemed to me.”

In a number of writings Psellos developed the ideal of the “political man,” who was less a perfect courtier than an enlightened public servant who could mediate between rival claims for the good of all.
The retired functionary Ioannes Zonaras thought of public affairs as being “in the middle” of things.
That space was not owned by any one person.

zh: 皇帝名义上主管
的公共空间，但只是作为其监护者而非所有者。有些不止名义上主管，并对其“行政”与“管理”亲自关心，这大概是翻译术语
与
的最佳方式，
这两个词在所有涉及政治的史料中无处不在。
总是
，要么是 κοινά、κοινὰ πράγματα、κράτος 等的，
正如皇帝总是被理解为
皇帝，而非仅凭自身权利的皇帝。
在一部
中，利奥三世自称“
的监护者”或“管家”。
Psellos 对在其兄弟米海尔四世治下治理帝国的孤儿院总管约安尼斯有一个妙喻：“他自任拉起罗马车轴”，仿佛政体是一辆战车。
这些隐喻是试图把共同属于所有罗马人的政治领域实体化。这本质上就是君士坦丁十一世·帕莱奥洛格斯1453年拒绝交出君士坦丁堡时所表示的。这位末代罗马皇帝的临终之言包括：“我无权把君士坦丁堡交给你们，城中任何居民也无此权。依集体决定（κοινῇ γνώμῃ），我们全体将自愿赴死，而不试图保命。”
西塞罗会在这其中认出
en: Emperors were nominally in charge of the public space of the
but only as its custodians, not its owners. Some were more than nominally in charge and took a personal interest in its “administration” and “management,” probably the best way to translate the terms
and
which are pervasive in all sources that refer to politics. The
was always
either of the κοινά, the κοινὰ πράγματα, the κράτος, and so on,
in the same way that the emperor was always understood to be the emperor
and not simply emperor in his own right.
In a
Leon III called himself the “guardian” or “steward of the
Psellos has a nice image for Ioannes Orphanotrophos, who governed the empire under his brother Michael IV: “he took it upon himself to pull the Roman axle,” as if the polity were a chariot.

These metaphors were attempts to reify a political sphere that belonged to all Romans collectively. That is essentially what Konstantinos XI Palaiologos signified when he refused to surrender the City in 1453. Among the last words of this last Roman emperor were, “I do not have the right to give you the City, nor does anyone else of those who live in it. By a collective decision (κοινῇ γνώμῃ), we will all willingly die and not try to save our lives.”
Cicero would have recognized in this the

zh: 权力行使中的公共与私人
en: Public versus Private in the Exercise of Power

zh: 罗马法的一条在拜占庭运作的基本原则是，“一切人类财物要么公共（δημόσια）要么私人。公共者不属于任何人而属于共同体；私人者分别属于各人。”
相应地有“公法与私法之分。公法关乎
之建制，私法关乎个人利益。”
en: It was a basic principle of Roman law, operative in Byzantium, that “all human goods are either public (δημόσια) or private. The public ones belong to no one but the community; the private ones belong to each person separately.”
There were, accordingly, distinctions between “public and private law. Public law is that which respects the establishment of the
private that which respects individuals’ interests.”

zh: 例如，“公共仪式代表人民以公共费用举行”，而“私人仪式为个人、家庭与家户举行。”
公共权威源于职位而非个人。
如我们所见，自共和国与奥古斯都时代（在其
希腊语版中）以及拜占庭，翻译
的方式之一是 τὰ δημόσια πράγματα 或仅 τὰ πράγματα，可扩展为 ῾Ρωμαϊκὰ πράγματα 再缩略为 τὰ ῾Ρωμαϊκά。与现代主义理论家关于前现代政体个人性质的常规断言相反，
在罗马传统中没有什么比
更“公共”，它不可能私下属于皇帝。甚至
的基础设施——例如宫殿——也不属于他，我们将看到皇帝与作者都承认这一点。两大帝国国库之一甚至被称为 τὸ δημόσιον，强化了这一点。
这是不存在皇位继承权的原因之一：不归私人所有的东西不能作为遗产传下去。

如我们将见，此种转移只能通过民众欢呼拥立完成（而人民可通过“去拥立”收回那些权利）。我们将在第4、5章讨论主权及其转移，届时转向政权共和基础在历史时间中的政治后果。我在此的目的是勾勒关于公共事务的规范性共和意识形态。当我们终于有一部考察皇帝实际做了什么及其权力目的与界限的皇帝职位研究时，它将表明他们一般确依一种监护意识形态行事：他们是一个不属于他们的政体的管家。他们有机会滥用权力，但这有后果。在拜占庭，这些后果常是血腥的。
en: For example, “public rituals are performed on behalf of the people at public expense,” while “private rituals are performed for individual men, families, and households.”
Public authority stemmed from the office, not the man personally.
As we have seen, since the days of the Republic and Augustus (in the Greek version of his
), as also in Byzantium, one way to translate

was τὰ δημόσια πράγματα or simply τὰ πράγματα, which could be expanded to ῾Ρωμαϊκὰ πράγματα and then abbreviated as τὰ ῾Ρωμαϊκά. Contrary to what is routinely asserted by modernist theorists regarding the personal nature of premodern polities,
nothing could be more “public” in the Roman tradition than the
which could not belong to the emperor privately. Not even the infrastructure of the
—for example, the palace—belonged to him, and we will see both emperors and authors conceding the point. One of the two main imperial treasuries was even called τὸ δημόσιον, reinforcing the point.
This was one of the reasons why there existed no right of succession to the throne: what was not owned privately could not be bequeathed.

As we will see, such transference could be accomplished only by popular acclamation (and the people could take back those rights through “deacclamation”). We will discuss the sovereignty and its transference in Chapters 4 and 5, when we turn to the political consequences in historical time of the regime’s republican basis. My purpose here is to outline the normative republican ideology about public issues. When we finally get a study of the imperial office that examines what the emperors actually did and the purpose and limits of their power, it will show that they generally did behave in accordance with an ideology of custodianship: they were the stewards of a polity that did not belong to them. They had opportunity to abuse their power, but this had consequences. In Byzantium, they were often bloody.

zh: 如下一节将见，皇帝抓住一切可能机会宣称其统治专为臣民利益。他们也定期提醒臣民帝国资产指定用于公共而非皇帝“私人”使用。566年查士丁二世解释说“我们臣民缴纳的税部分用于他们自身、部分间接为他们而花费，因为我们从中不获任何利益，只受托管理。”
提比略二世（578–582年在位）在一部
中指出“应当认为帝国地产的资产不单是我们的，而是我们
的公共财产
罗曼努斯一世在 934年颁布的
中禁止官员和其他有权势者取得受保护土地，并指出违犯者须“把获取之价付给国库，不是为了国库的利润或进项——因为我们怎能在一心遏制他人无尽贪欲之时，无耻地为自身之利（οἰκεῖον κέρδος）颁布此令，显得自己不是为共同善（κοινῆν ὠφέλειαν）而是为私利行事？——而是为了照顾穷人。”
即便在此情形中，皇帝所指也不是其私人利益而是
的利益（后者本身即公共善）；钱将直接交归公共使用。在其一部
（996年）中，巴西尔二世也“把自己呈现为国库财产权的监护者以及受法律授权保护它们的权威。”
他在此与国库的关系只是一种广泛构想的、针对整个政体的管家意识形态的一个面向。个人不被等同于职位，而职位相对于共同善被定义。十三世纪时尼基弗鲁斯·布莱米德斯（Nikephoros Blemmydes）同样“推理说皇帝不私下持有任何东西，因为他不是私人个体，而是为共同体（τὸ κοινόν）之益管理公共财富（τὰ κοινὰ）。”
en: As we will see in the following section, emperors took every possible opportunity to proclaim that they ruled solely for the benefit of their subjects. They also periodically reminded their subjects that imperial assets were destined for public use, not the “private” use by emperors. In 566, Justin II explained that “the taxes paid by our subjects are used and expended partly for themselves and partly indirectly on their account, for we do not derive any benefit from them and are only charged with their administration.”
Tiberios II (578–582 AD) noted in a
that “it is fitting to consider that the assets of imperial properties are not ours alone but are the common property
of our
In his

of 934 barring office-holders and other powerful interests from acquiring protected lands, Romanos I noted that violators were to “pay the price of the acquisition to the treasury, not for the profit of or contribution to the treasury—for how could we, in our endeavors to restrain the insatiable covetousness of others, shamelessly issue this ruling for our own gain (οἰκεῖον κέρδος) and show ourselves to be guilty of acting not for the common good (κοινῆν ὠφέλειαν) but for our own?—but for the care of the poor.”
Even in this case, the emperor does not mean his own private benefit but that of the
(itself a public good); the money will rather be given over directly to public use. In one of his
(996 AD), Basileios II also “presents himself as a custodian of the fisc’s property rights and as the legally empowered authority to protect them.”

His relation to the fisc here was only one aspect of a broadly conceived ideology of stewardship with respect to the entire polity. The person was not identified with the office, and the office was defined in relation to the common good. In the thirteenth century, Nikephoros Blemmydes likewise “reasoned that the emperor held nothing in private because he was not a private individual, but administered public wealth (τὰ κοινὰ) for the benefit of the community (τὸ κοινόν).”

zh: 与这些皇帝同时代的史家批评皇帝把公共资金浪费于私人目的。Euagrios（六世纪晚）认为查士丁尼是坏皇帝，批评他建许多教堂，并提醒那些想这么做的人“用自己的资源”付钱。
大概他指用现有帝国资金即不征新税，但也可能指私人资产。Skylitzes 批评米海尔四世花“公共与共同资金”行虔诚之事以赎其登上皇位所犯之罪：“他在用别人的钱买自己的忏悔”，Skylitzes 说，指罗马人的钱。
Psellos 批评君士坦丁九世把帝国国库的钱花在他对斯克勒莱娜（Skleraina）的迷恋上，后来又浪费更多在其阿兰情妇身上，也批评佐伊（Zoe）与塞奥多拉掏空国库给宠臣送礼。
在这些情形中，统治者被指控以不益于罗马人民的方式花公共钱。
en: Contemporary historians criticized emperors for wasting public funds on private purposes. Euagrios (late sixth century), who believed that Justinian was a bad emperor, criticized his building of many churches and reminded those who would do the same to pay for them “from their own resources.”

Presumably he means from existing imperial funds, that is, no new taxes, but he may be referring to private assets. Skylitzes criticized Michael IV for spending “public and common funds” in order to perform pious deeds and earn forgiveness for the crimes by which he had ascended the throne: “he was buying his own repentance with the money of others,” said Skylitzes, meaning the money of the Romans.

Psellos criticized Konstantinos IX for spending money from the imperial treasury on his passion for Skleraina and later for wasting more on his Alan mistress, and he also criticized Zoe and Theodora for emptying the treasury to give presents to their favorites.
In these cases, rulers were being accused of spending public money in ways that did not benefit the Roman people.

zh: 其他体裁也反映这一意识形态。我先举九世纪一例再转向十二世纪科穆宁政权史家。
属于学者称为“君主之镜”的体裁。该体裁存世样本众多，其主要特征之一是提醒皇帝其唯一职责是促进公共善而非为私利统治。为统治者而非被统治者之益统治在所有这些文本中是僭主制的定义。
在这部致利奥六世的文本中，皇帝被提醒不要过于看重物质财富。“此外，你的财产并非真正你自己的，而属于同你一样为上帝服役的人，尤其穷人与外人。所以在
之事上要留心表现为施恩者。”
诚然这劝诫背后是一切财富属上帝的观念（虽未明言），但这只强化了共和传统加于皇帝的管家角色。罗马与基督教观念在此汇合。同一点后来以不同方式表述：“宫殿今天属于你但明天将不；后天它将属于别人，再后天属于其后之人，以致它从不属于任何人。因为尽管它频繁易手，它没有真正的主人。”
从永恒视角看这当然最终可用于任何类型财产，但它在此服务于强化一条政治公理。
en: Other genres reflect this ideology too. I will present an example from the ninth century and then turn to the historians of the Komnenoi regime in the twelfth century. The

children: Hortatory Chapters Addressed to Leon VI

en: belongs to the genre that scholars call Mirrors of Princes. One of the main features of this genre, of which many specimens survive, was to remind emperors that their sole duty was to promote the public good and not to rule for their private benefit. Ruling for the benefit of the ruler rather than the ruled was the definition of tyranny in all these texts.

In this text addressed to Leon VI, the emperor is reminded not to place too much value on material wealth. “Besides, your property is not really your own but belongs to your fellow slaves [i.e., of God], especially the poor and outsiders. So take care to emerge as a benefactor when it comes to the

To be sure, behind this exhortation lies the notion that all wealth belongs to God (though it is not stated explicitly), but this only reinforces the role of steward that the republican tradition imposed on the emperor. Roman and Christian notions here converged. The same point is later made differently: “The palace belongs to you today but tomorrow it will not; and after tomorrow it will belong to someone else, and the day after that to the one after him, so that it never belongs to anyone. For even though it changes hands often, it has no true owner.”
From the vantage-point of eternity this, of course, could ultimately be said about any type of property, but it serves to reinforce a political axiom here.

zh: 要看到这一观点的非神学式有力表达，我们转向科穆宁时代，其王朝式统治扰动了传统假设，从而暴露了先前被视为当然的东西。现代史家已表明科穆宁政权如何把帝国推向个人或家族统治，其中血缘比职位更重要。
时人注意到共同体的公共事务与皇帝个人所掌事务之间、共和国所有者与监护者之间区分的侵蚀。并非他们突然重新发现共和价值，
而是他们感知到先前主导的价值正被科穆宁式统治侵蚀，并为之痛心。早在阿莱克修斯一世（1081–1118）统治之初，安条克主教约安尼斯·奥克塞特斯（Ioannes Oxeites）就向皇帝抱怨“你的亲属正成为对
与我们其余所有人的大瘟疫……他们更关心为自己牟利而非共同利益（κοινῇ）。”约安尼斯劝阿莱克修斯“凡事依军队、教会与所有其他人民[即
]中最优秀者的建议而行……并把你的审议置于中间（εἰς μέσον）。”
en: For robust nontheological expressions of this view, we turn to the era of the Komnenoi, whose dynastic manner of rule disturbed traditional assumptions and so exposed what had previously been taken for granted. Modern historians have shown how the regime of the Komnenoi pushed the empire in the direction of personal or family rule, where blood mattered more than office.
Contemporaries noted the erosion of the distinction between public and imperial and between owner and custodian of the republic. It was not that they suddenly rediscovered republican values,

but they perceived that previously dominant values were being undermined by the Komnenian style of rule, and deplored it. Already at the beginning of the reign of Alexios I (1081–1118), Ioannes Oxeites, bishop of Antioch, complained to the emperor that “your relatives are proving to be a great pestilence upon both the

and all the rest of us... they are more concerned with making a profit for themselves than with the common interest (κοινῇ).” Ioannes advises Alexios to “do everything with the advice of the best men in the army, the Church, and all the other people [i.e., the
]... and place your deliberations in the middle (εἰς μέσον).”

zh: 这正是佐纳拉斯用来指其政治生涯的术语，
而正是他表述了对新政权的共和式批评。佐纳拉斯赞扬阿莱克修斯的道德品质但补充说对统治者应有更多期待，后者：
en: That was the very term that Zonaras had used to refer to his political career,
and it was he who articulated a republican critique of the new regime. Zonaras praises Alexios’s moral qualities but adds that more is to be expected from a ruler, who:

zh: 还须关心正义、为臣民的需要作打算、维护
的古老原则。但阿莱克修斯的议程是改变
的古老形式……他处理政治事务不仿佛它们是共同（κοινά）或公共（δημόσια）的，也不自视为其管家（οἰκονόμος）而是其主人（δεσπότης）。他认为宫殿是其私宅并如此称呼……他不按功绩各予其份，而是把公共钱成车地交给亲属与仆从。
en: must also care for justice, provide for his subjects, and maintain the ancient principles of the
But Alexios’ agenda was to alter the ancient forms of the

... He approached political affairs not as if they were common (κοινά) or public (δημόσια), and he did not regard himself to be their steward (οἰκονόμος) but their master (δεσπότης). He thought that the palace was his own private house and called it that... He did not give to each his own based on merit but rather gave over public money to his relatives and servants by the cartload.

zh: 这一批评只有在佐纳拉斯预期其读者同情他所勾勒的共和价值时才成立。佐纳拉斯批评若干其他皇帝把公共资金用于私人目的。
他恰好相信他所处时代不久以前发生了一场革命性转变。写到君士坦丁堡的建立时，他注意到占星家瓦伦斯（Valens）的预言：新都将延续696年。
en: The critique works only if Zonaras expected his readership to sympathize with the republican values he outlines. Zonaras criticized a number of other emperors for spending public funds for their own private purposes.

He happened to believe that recent history had witnessed a revolutionary transformation. Writing about the foundation of Constantinople, he notes the prediction of the astrologer Valens that the new capital would last for 696 years.

zh: 但这些年限如今早已过去，以致我们要么须视其预言为假、其术为有缺陷，要么须设想他指的是
诸形式连同恰当礼制得以维持的年数，那时元老院受尊荣、其公民繁荣，那时会有合法监督（ἔννομος ἐπιστασία），
而政权将是
而非僭主制——后者即统治者把共同之物（κοινά）视为己有并用于私人享乐之时。
en: But these have now long since passed, so that we must either regard his prediction as false and his art as flawed or we must suppose that he meant the years during which the forms of the
would be maintained along with the proper protocols, when the senate would be honored, its citizens would flourish, when there would be a lawful supervision (ἔννομος ἐπιστασία),
and the regime would be a
rather than a tyranny, when the rulers would consider that common things (κοινά) were their own and use them for their private pleasures.

zh: 尼基塔斯·科尼亚特斯对曼努埃尔·科穆宁提出类似批评。他说统治者“爱把公共钱（τὰ δημόσια）当作自己的私产挥霍，并把自由人当作奴隶对待。”
en: Niketas Choniates leveled similar criticisms against Manuel Komnenos. Rulers, he says, “love to squander the public money (τὰ δημόσια) as if it were their own private patrimony and treat free men as their slaves.”

zh: 当然科穆宁家族上台时并无实施激进反共和议程的意图，我们必须对佐纳拉斯的批评持保留态度，因为他似乎正属于家族接管时失势的那些阶层。科穆宁家族未废除
；至少他们、且大概其多数臣民不这么认为。他们的治理体系虽更个人化，却是应对一系列危机而发展起来的，而且这套制度确有一功：它使
免遭外敌摧毁。然而佐纳拉斯批评的语汇揭示了他与其他人所认为的共识：关于皇帝对公共信托的责任以及私人利益与公共利益之区分。保罗·马格达利诺在对佐纳拉斯批评的分析中表明，科穆宁家族及其代言人并未坚持一种不同的
或
模型，而是依传统理由为政权辩护（尽管他们掩盖了已发生的变化）。
因此不存在意识形态断裂：科穆宁家族基本宣称自己是与前任无异的罗马皇帝。此外 Dimiter Angelov 表明，帕莱奥洛格斯时期的许多作者同样依皇帝们多么尽责地维护公共利益之完整来评价他们，该利益由臣民托付给他们而不私人地属于他们。
en: The Komnenoi, of course, did not come to power with the intention of implementing a radical, antirepublican agenda, and we must take Zonaras’s criticisms with a grain of salt, as he seems to have belonged to the very classes that lost power when the family took over. The Komnenoi did not abolish the

at least they, and probably most of their subjects, did not think so. Their system of governance, more personal though it was, developed in response to a series of crises and can be credited with saving the

from foreign enemies. The terms of Zonaras’s critique, however, reveal what he and others believed the consensus was regarding the responsibilities of the emperor toward the public trust and the distinction between private and public interests. In his analysis of Zonaras’s critique, Paul Magdalino has shown that the Komnenoi and their spokesmen did not uphold a different model of either the
or the
but rather defended the regime on traditional grounds (for all that they glossed over the changes that had taken place).

There was, then, no ideological rift: the Komnenoi were basically claiming to be Roman emperors no different than their predecessors. Moreover, Dimiter Angelov has shown that many authors of the Palaiologan period likewise evaluated their emperors on how conscientiously they maintained the integrity of the public interest, which was entrusted to them by their subjects and did not belong to them personally.

zh: 这种帝国“监护”观可追溯到帝国最早期。提比略一世曾宣称士兵不属于他自己而属于公共（δημόσιοι），马可·奥勒留则声称国库属于元老院与人民：“况且我们所住的是你们的房子。”
我们可能不免想把这视为单纯修辞或“高调理论”，
但事实上它是一种根深蒂固的共和意识形态，在任何历史时刻都与
不可分离。诚然这些及其他皇帝的陈述不澄清权力事实——那才是许多史家真正想要的，故有轻蔑语汇。但我们应更小心。我们不能把一种在共和国结束一千多年后似乎仍兴旺——即塑造关于权力行使的基本假设——的意识形态当作修辞浮沫或共和“残余”一笔勾销。若如此勾销，须被当作单纯残余勾销的拜占庭信念与实践清单会相当长。
替代做法是把它们归为一组并认识到拜占庭政体一直确由一种共和式罗马意识形态塑造。该意识形态支配臣民如何评价其统治者，从而支配他们在关键时刻如何行事，而这些时刻在拜占庭历史上比许多人意识到的更频繁。在危机时刻，那些底层假设浮现到前台。
en: This view of imperial “custodianship” goes back to the earliest days of the empire. Tiberius I once declared that the soldiers belonged not to himself but to the public (δημόσιοι), and Marcus Aurelius professed that the fisc belonged to the senate and people: “moreover, it is your house in which we live.”
We might be tempted to dismiss this as mere rhetoric or as “high-flown theory,”
but in reality it was a deeply rooted republican ideology that was inseparable from the

at any point in history. To be sure, the statements made by these and other emperors do not clarify the facts of power, which is what many historians are really after, whence the dismissive language. But we should be more careful. We cannot write off as rhetorical fluff or as a republican “remnant” an ideology that seemed to be thriving—that is, shaping fundamental assumptions about the exercise of power—a thousand and more years after the end of the Republic. The list of Byzantine beliefs and practices that would have to be written off in this way as mere remnants would be quite long.

The alternative is to group them together and realize that the Byzantine polity was really shaped by a republican Roman ideology all along. This ideology governed how subjects evaluated their rulers and consequently how they behaved in critical circumstances, which were more frequent in Byzantine history than many realize. In moments of crisis, those underlying assumptions came to the fore.

zh: （而且，若我们要把据称不影响帝国权力冷硬事实的意识形态当作“单纯修辞”勾销，那么首先该勾销的应是皇帝由上帝任命统治并有义务模仿基督的观念。）
en: (Also, if we were to dismiss as “mere rhetoric” ideologies that allegedly do not bear on the cold hard facts of imperial power, then the first to go should be the idea that the emperor was appointed to rule by God and had a duty to imitate Christ.)

zh: 私人利益与公共利益之区分反映于作家如何评价各级任官者包括皇帝。阿米安努斯（Ammianus）批评瓦伦提尼安把家庭置于共同善之上，选其弟瓦伦斯与他共掌帝国，但赞许他后来决定不进军援助瓦伦斯对抗叛乱者普罗科匹乌斯，因为后者只是其弟的敌人而阿勒曼尼人是整个罗马世界的敌人。
Prokopios 说贝利撒留“被所有罗马人唾骂，因为他为了自家的事，牺牲了
最急切的利益。”
皇帝君士坦丁十世强迫其妻欧多基亚（Eudokia）发誓在他死后（1067年）不再嫁，但后来她、元老院与牧首一致同意应以对整体的预先考虑为指导标准：共同善优先于一个将死之人的私人愿望是合理的。不可能允许私人愿望压倒公共善。于是人们认识到，因一个人过于嫉妒而不让其遗孀与另一男人在一起从而导致没有皇帝，会损害共同善并促成罗马帝国的毁灭。这一看法占了上风。
en: The distinction between private and public interest is reflected in how writers evaluated office-holders of all ranks, including emperors. Ammianus criticizes Valentinian for putting family over the common good when he chose his brother Valens as his partner in empire, but approves his decision later not to march to Valens’s aid against the rebel Procopius because the latter was an enemy only of his brother whereas the Alamanni were the enemies of the entire Roman world.
Prokopios says that Belisarios was “reviled by all the Romans for sacrificing the most critical needs of the
to his domestic affairs.”

The emperor Konstantinos X forced his wife Eudokia to swear that she would not remarry after his death (in 1067), but then she, the senate, and the patriarch agreed that forethought on behalf of the whole should be their guiding criterion: it was reasonable for the common good to be preferred over the private wish of one man who was about to die. It was not possible to allow a private wish to override the public good. Thus it was recognized that not to have an emperor because one man was too jealous to allow his widow to be with another man would harm the common good and contribute to the destruction of the Roman empire. This view of the matter prevailed.

zh: 十二世纪晚，塞萨洛尼基的尤斯塔西奥斯在1185年诺曼围城期间痛斥其城总督大卫·科穆宁（David Komnenos）“忽视并蔑视共同善、只谋自身福祉，像个公开的叛徒。”当其个人地位变得危殆时，他还“把眼看就要落到自己头上的灾难，转嫁给我们整个共同体。”
en: In the late twelfth century, Eustathios of Thessalonike castigated the governor of his city, David Komnenos, during the Norman siege of 1185 for “neglecting and despising the common good and looking only to his own welfare, like an open traitor.” When his personal position became precarious, he continued to “replace the private disaster which menaced him with one which would affect our whole community.”

zh: 十一世纪晚，Attaleiates 在努力解释其时代崩溃时批评了整个帝国最高指挥层。
en: Attaleiates, in the late eleventh century, criticized the entire imperial high command in his effort to explain the collapse of his times.

zh: 至于我们时代的罗马人，其领袖与皇帝以公共利益为借口（προφάσει δημοσιακῆς ὠφελείας）犯下最恶劣的罪行与上帝憎恶之行。军队统帅对战争毫不在意，也不做对其祖国（τῇ πατρίδι）正当恰当之事，甚至蔑视胜利之荣耀；相反他全心逐利，把指挥权变成一桩买卖，因而不给自己的人民（τοῦ ἰδίου ἔθνους）带来繁荣或荣耀。
en: As for the Romans of our times, their leaders and emperors commit the worst crimes and God-detested deeds under the pretext of the public interest (προφάσει δημοσιακῆς ὠφελείας). The commander of the army cares not one whit for the war nor does what is right and proper by his fatherland (τῇ πατρίδι), and even shows contempt for the glory of victory; instead, he bends his whole self to the making of profit, converting his command into a mercantile venture, and so he brings no prosperity or glory to his own people (τοῦ ἰδίου ἔθνους).

zh: “公共利益”的意识形态至上性在此尤为明显，因为这些皇帝与将军似乎留心援引它，即使在这位史家看来他们实际在服务私人利益。在拜占庭，一切国家行动都必须依公共利益、相对于祖国与罗马人民来证成，哪怕只是借口。Attaleiates 指出，相反古罗马人“不追求金钱与财富之获取，而只追求声望、其男子气概之展现、以及其国家的安全与辉煌。”
en: The ideological supremacy of the “public interest” is evident here especially, as it seems that these emperors and generals took care to invoke it even when, in this historian’s opinion, they were really serving their private interests. In Byzantium, all state action had to be justified on the grounds of the public interest, in relation to the fatherland and the Roman people, even if only as a pretext. The Romans of old, by contrast, Attaleiates points out, “did not strive for money and acquisition of wealth but simply for renown, the demonstration of their manliness, and their country’s safety and splendor.”

zh: 我们考察的文本反映对共同善与公共利益的强烈献身。显然关于它究竟是什么及如何最好支持它会有强烈分歧——那正是政治的内容——但对我们重要的是帝国政策必须参照它来证成，且它被感知为分离于皇帝与其官员的私人利益。举两个诉诸公共善的例子：当牧首尼古拉斯·米斯蒂科斯（Nikolaos Mystikos，十世纪初）试图说服一位世俗官员不要在战时压力下实施教会行政变更时，他先依什么会取悦上帝论证，最后以此作结：“
无疑不会从教士被征入军队或教会照料的穷人被沦为奴隶中获得任何利益。”
译者再次把
译作“国家”，但那更不通：所议改革正是为了国家利益而考虑的。尼古拉斯诉诸一个更宽更高的标准，即
与共同善的标准。
en: The texts we have surveyed reflect a strong devotion to the common good and the public interest. Obviously, there would have been strong disagreements about what it was exactly and how to best support it—that was the stuff of politics—but what matters for us here is that imperial policy had to be justified by reference to it and that it was perceived to be separate from the private interests of both the emperor and his officials. To give two examples of the appeal to the public good, when the patriarch Nikolaos Mystikos (in the early tenth century) was trying to persuade a secular official not to implement an administrative change in the Church under wartime pressure, he argues first based on what would please God and concludes with this: “Surely the
will derive no profit whatever either from clerics being enlisted in the army or from the poor of the Church being reduced to slavery.”
The translators again render
as “state,” but that makes less sense: the reforms in question were being considered precisely to benefit the state. Nikolaos was appealing to a broader and higher standard, that of the
and the common good.

zh: 1057年即位时，伊萨克·科穆宁认定国家预算过于臃肿于是削减，尤其削减有头衔者的俸给。这引起广泛不满。支持这些削减的 Psellos 要我们相信它们最终被接受，“因为面对有意批评这项政策的人，以公共利益〔或国库，ὁ δημόσιος〕为由，已经足以为这些削减辩护。”
若我们能信 Psellos，这算拜占庭政治成熟的一例：危机时刻私人利益为公共善牺牲。但 Psellos 是否说真话并不重要：重要的是他选择用来框定其政策辩护的语汇。在拜占庭政治行动能据以证成的唯一语汇就是这些。在此我们触及我所定义的意识形态。
en: When he took the throne in 1057, Isaakios Komnenos decided that the state budget was too bloated and so he made cutbacks, especially in payments to title-holders. This caused widespread disaffection. Psellos, who supported these cuts, would have us believe that eventually they were accepted “because the public interest [or treasury: ὁ δημόσιος] was a sufficient justification of them against those who wanted to criticize this policy.”

If we can trust Psellos, this would count as an instance of political maturity in Byzantium, private interests being sacrificed for the public good in a moment of crisis. But it does not matter whether Psellos is telling the truth: what counts are the terms in which he chose to frame his defense of the policy. The only terms by which political action could be justified in Byzantium were these. Here we are accessing what I have defined as ideology.

zh: 罗曼尼亚在我们文本中呈现为一个非人格实体，其需要证成帝国行动。在给一座修道院的豁免授予中，阿莱克修斯一世甚至提到可能征水手服役的帝国官员“因罗曼尼亚的紧迫需要（κατά τινα ἀναγκαιοτάτην χρείαν τῆς ῾Ρωμανίας）。”
民族国家在此被人格化。外交政策亦然。阿莱克修斯许诺威尼斯人任何他们想要的以换取对抗诺曼人的帮助，“只要不违背罗马国家的利益。”
这呼应古罗马的
在
）序言中，君士坦丁七世解释他想教儿子如何“在关系到最妥善的谋略与共同利益（τὸ κοινῇ συμφέρον）的事上不犯错：首先，每个民族在何事上有能力益于罗马人、在何事上有害。”
我们缺乏一项关于拜占庭人如何解析其外交政策道德的研究——他们被困于“国家理性”（reasons of state）与基督教伦理之间。公共利益多久压倒其他考虑一次？公共利益的道德逻辑是否不同于私人生活？有理由认为如此，但我们需要完整研究。例如帝国官员似乎参与异教仪式甚至献祭，或承认其有效，以与蛮族缔结必要同盟。
这违反共和国的宗教规范以维护其对外利益。此外 Psellos
中有一段明确在杜卡斯派系（Psellos 当时所属）刺瞎罗曼努斯四世·第欧根尼一事上提出此问题。他在那里承认这是可怕罪行但相信必须为之：“一件本不该发生、但——用稍异方式重复我刚说的——

children: 不惜一切代价必须发生

zh: 之事：前者出于虔诚与对残忍的宗教顾虑，后者出于 τὰ πράγματα 的状态与时刻的危殆。”
en: Romanía appears in our texts as an impersonal entity whose needs justify imperial actions. In a grant of exemptions to a monastery, Alexios I even refers to imperial officials who might draft sailors into service “because of the pressing needs of Romanía (κατά τινα ἀναγκαιοτάτην χρείαν τῆς ῾Ρωμανίας).”

The nation-state is here personalized. Likewise in foreign policy. Alexios promised the Venetians whatever they wanted in exchange for help against the Normans, “so long as it was not against the interests of the Roman state.”
This echoes the ancient Roman
In the preface of the

Konstantinos VII explains that he wants to teach his son how “not to stumble concerning the best counsels and the common interests (τὸ κοινῇ συμφέρον): first, in what each nation has power to advantage the Romans and in what to hurt.”

We lack a study of how Byzantines parsed the morality of their foreign policy, trapped between “reasons of state” and Christian ethics. How often did the public interest trump other considerations? Was the moral logic of the public interest different from that of private life? There is reason to think so, but we need a full study. For example, imperial officials seem to have taken part in pagan rituals and even sacrifices, or recognized them as valid, in order to seal necessary alliances with barbarian peoples.
This violated the religious norms of the republic to safeguard its foreign interests. There is, moreover, a passage in Psellos’s

that raises this issue explicitly in relation to the blinding of Romanos IV Diogenes by the Doukas faction to which Psellos now belonged. He there admits that this was a horrible crime but believed that it had to be done: “an action which should not have happened, but—to repeat what I just said in only a slightly different way—which

children: had to happen at all costs:

en: the former on account of piety and religious scruple against cruelty, the latter on account of the state of τὰ πράγματα and the precariousness of the moment.”

zh: 在讨论早期现代非人格国家的出现时，哈维·曼斯菲尔德（Harvey Mansfield）解释“为国家做道德上令人反感之事获得一种道德豁免，因为此类行动不再自私。这当然只是把自私推及更大的范围，况且理由也经不起推敲，因为国家事实上总有所属。”
Psellos 要我们相信他所指的
——要求刺瞎罗曼努斯的共同利益——属于罗马人，后者需要走出内战并整顿小亚细亚；但当然受益者是当时控制国家的杜卡斯家族。现代行政权力的使用呈现完全相同的含混。“意识形态”正位于诉诸共同善以证成益于私人利益之行动处，而私人利益本身无立足之地。它们只是历史事实，但需要意识形态掩护才能成为可接受的政治现实。
en: In discussing the emergence of the impersonal state in early modernity, Harvey Mansfield explains how “doing something morally distasteful for the state acquires a moral exemption because such actions are no longer selfish. They are, of course, generalized selfishness and specious too, since the state does in fact belong to somebody.”
Psellos wants us to believe that the

to which he refers, the common interests that required Romanos to be blinded, belonged to the Romans, who needed to get past the civil war and put Asia Minor in order; but of course, the beneficiaries were the Doukai, who controlled the state at that moment. The use of modern executive power presents exactly the same ambiguities. “Ideology” is located precisely in the invocation of the common good to justify actions that benefit private interests, which had no standing on their own. They were but historical facts but needed ideological cover to become acceptable political reality.

zh: 我们已走得比必要更远。本节旨在表明的只是：拜占庭人在规范意义上把其
构想为一个集体但非人格的实体，其需要压倒私人利益，甚至、尤其皇帝的私人利益。只需花些时间读拜占庭史料，就不难察觉这种观念。该领域的问题一直是如何绕过它。例如吉尔贝·达格龙承认“帝国独立于上台并试图建立王朝的皇帝而存在。它以罗马式的庞大行政与法律构造形式存在，君主支配它并确保其凝聚，却从不与之完全等同。”皇帝职位与担任该职者有明确的区别，“一如今天般鲜明。”
但达格龙的研究不致力于此题，而是关于皇帝是否因僭取某些祭司职能而感到内疚的深奥问题。结果他几乎只相对于旧约模型而非罗马模型来读皇帝职位。
en: We have gone further than necessary. All this section aimed to show is that the Byzantines conceived their

in a normative sense as a collective but impersonal entity whose needs trumped private interests, even, or especially, those of the emperor. It is not hard to detect this ideology if one but spends a moderate amount of time in the company of Byzantine sources. The problem for the field has been how to get around it. Gilbert Dagron, for instance, recognized that “the empire existed independently of the emperor who came to power and who attempted to found a dynasty. It existed in the Roman form of a vast administrative and juridical construction which the sovereign dominated and whose cohesion he ensured without ever becoming entirely identified with it.” A distinction was drawn, “as sharply as today, between the imperial office and its holder.”

But Dagron’s study is not devoted to this topic, being rather about the esoteric question of whether the emperor felt guilty for usurping some sacerdotal functions. As a result, he reads the imperial office almost exclusively in relation to Old Testament models rather than Roman ones.

zh: 保罗·马格达利诺也对基本要点作出了准确而雄辩的表述：
en: Paul Magdalino also produced an accurate and eloquent formulation of the basic point:

zh: 无疑拜占庭人相信并体验国家为一件非人格的公共事务——一个
。财政体系、常备军与法庭构成一个制度组合，多于维系它的个人纽带之和。皇帝授予的尊位和薪俸被视为人们凭功绩取得的权利，只有犯下死罪才会丧失。各级显贵大可自许是服务公众的官员，而非皇帝的家臣，不是廷臣而是元老，其个人与集体荣誉由一种传统秩序
与既定程序
保障，皇帝与他们同样受其约束。
en: There can be no doubt that the Byzantines believed in and experienced the state as an impersonal, public affair—a

The fiscal system, the standing army and the law courts formed an institutional ensemble which was more than the sum of the personal ties that held it together. The dignities and salaries bestowed by the emperor were perceived as rights which men deserved by their merits and forfeited only by committing capital crimes. The hierarchy of dignitaries could flatter themselves that they were not imperial but public servants, not courtiers but senators, whose individual and collective honor was guaranteed by a traditional order
and established procedure
to which the emperor was as committed as they were.

zh: 不幸马格达利诺随后声称这一切“只存在于浸淫古代史的知识分子的心智与言辞中”，从而削弱这幅图景。这是拜占庭学领域的一种反射本能：凡显得太古典或太罗马者必须被淡化、边缘化或以其他方式限定。无论它是否是史料实际呈现的图景、这些原则是否由皇帝自己公开承认、或这些知识分子是否正是皇帝借以实际治理的法官、将军与主教，都不重要。马格达利诺再次指向个人关系：“很难区分公共职位与私人庇护。”但这适用于所有政体，包括现代的。私人利益与个人纽带在拜占庭一如今天重要，史家聚焦它们是对的。然而拜占庭人明白此类东西不构成其共和国，后者代表所有罗马人的共同事务与利益。
en: Unfortunately, Magdalino then goes on to undermine this picture by claiming that it all “existed only in the minds and words of intellectuals steeped in ancient history.” This is a reflex instinct in the field of Byzantine Studies: anything that seems too classical or too Roman must be downplayed, marginalized, or otherwise qualified. It does not matter whether it is the picture that actually emerges from the sources, that these principles were avowed by the emperors themselves, or that these intellectuals were the judges, generals, and bishops through whom the emperors actually governed. Magdalino again points to personal relations: “it is difficult to distinguish between the public office and the private patronage.” But this applies to all polities, modern ones too. Private interests and personal ties were as important in Byzantium as they are today, and historians are right to focus on them. Nevertheless, the Byzantines understood that such things did not constitute their republic, which represented the common affairs and interests of all the Romans.

zh: 君主制服务于共和国
en: The Monarchy Served the Republic

zh: 保罗·韦纳（Paul Veyne）曾论早期罗马帝国论证“国家即皇帝”，是其财产，且“他可以说
（朕即国家）。”
但没有皇帝——罗马或拜占庭——说过或暗示过类似的话，或暗示其统治出于益于其罗马同胞之外的任何目的或理由，且大体是物质上益于他们。这正是我们预期在共和政体中发现的，其中
被理解为人民的事务，韦纳后来在另一本书里，似乎转而认可了这一点。
这种对主权
的问责不是我们预期在如下政体中发现的：那里没有基于共识的统一政体观念，或权力由上帝授予君主以行上帝意志或干脆其自己意志。古希腊人如此想象波斯专制：若统治者行事恶劣，他不对任何其他人负责。
诚然拜占庭皇帝理应奉行上帝的旨意，但拜占庭上帝的意志是皇帝努力益于共和国，这并非巧合。事实上早期帝国下所有罗马职位——甚至最地方性的市政职位——的要求是，官长“受道德约束为城市共同体之善行事……公仆须公开宣誓将为城镇之善行事。”
en: Paul Veyne once argued, with reference to the early Roman empire, that “the state was the emperor,” that it was his property, and that “he could say,

But no emperor, Roman or Byzantine, ever said or implied anything like that, or suggested that he ruled for any purpose or reason other than to benefit his fellow Romans, and benefit them materially at that, for the most part. This is precisely what we expect to find in a republican regime, in which the
is understood to be the people’s business, and Veyne seems to have come around on that point in a later book.
This accountability to a sovereign

is not what we expect to find in regimes where there is no idea of a unified polity based on consensus or where power is bestowed by God for the monarch to do God’s will, or just his own. That was how the ancient Greeks imagined Persian despotism: if the ruler acted badly, he was not answerable to anyone else.

To be sure, the Byzantine emperor was expected to do God’s work, but it is no coincidence that the will of the Byzantine God was that the emperor work hard to benefit the republic. It was, in fact, a requirement of all Roman offices under the early empire, even the most local, municipal ones, that a magistrate was “under a moral constraint to act for the good of the urban community... Public servants were required to swear an oath in public that they would act for the good of the town.”

zh: 皇帝在这方面并无不同：其

en: The emperor was not different in this regard: his

zh: 历史上所有国王都被期望以某种方式益于臣民，但这不意味着其王国是共和国。为清楚理解罗马统治者的独特之处，值得离题谈被罗马取代的希腊化国王，因为他们提供了非共和统治的醒目模型（也因为他们常被奉为拜占庭皇帝的先例，在我看来是完全错误的假设）。希腊化王国可以说曾是国家或包含许多从属国家，但它们在任何意义上都不是统一的
。国王不能（也未）宣称主要或专为“一个人民”的利益行事。他们不依其所统治的具体政体被定义，因为他们不统治为促成一个
利益而构成的具体政体：其王国是领土、人民与城市的临时集合，涵盖不同类型的政治与法律实体。
后者可能脱离或被其他国王夺走并另谋出路。每个王国的组成部分作为独立法律实体互动，有时呈现令人困惑的图景。除马其顿国王部分例外，
希腊化国王不是任何特定东西——无论人民或领土——“的”国王；他们只被称为“国王”而无任何限定（如
），并与城市、人民及其他王国缔结个人条约。对这些国王的服务以个人语汇被理解，作为对一个人的纽带而非对非人格政体：国王的人是其“朋友”。
王位大体在王室内部承袭，国家机器是家产。国王也可从一个王国移到另一个，或机会主义地为自己开辟新领域。臣民理解国王主要为其自身利益行事，许多情形中作为剥削者。王室庇护有其好处，但国王至多被期望仅遵守条约、给臣民一些“恩惠”或“对他们善意”，而非为人民之益通宵工作。
他们本来就算不上“他的人民”。不存在服务
的概念，因为不存在

en: Historically all kings have been expected to benefit their subjects in some way, but this does not mean that their kingdoms were republics. To understand clearly what was distinctive about Roman rulers, it is worth digressing on the Hellenistic kings whom Rome replaced, because they offer striking models of nonrepublican rule (also because they are often upheld as precedents for the Byzantine emperors, in my view a thoroughly mistaken assumption). The Hellenistic kingdoms can be said to have been states, or to have subsumed many subordinate states, but they were not unified

in any sense. The kings could not (and did not) claim to be acting primarily or exclusively in the interest of “a people.” They were not defined in terms of the specific polities over which they ruled, because they did not rule over specific polities constituted to promote the interests of a
their kingdoms were ad hoc collections of territories, peoples, and cities, encompassing different types of political and legal entities.

The latter were liable to break off, or be stolen by other kings, and seek their fortunes elsewhere. The component parts of each kingdom interacted as separate legal entities, sometimes presenting a bewildering picture. With the partial exception of the kings of Macedonia,
the Hellenistic kings were not kings “of” anything in particular, whether a people or territory; they were just called “kings” without any qualification (e.g.,

), and they entered into personal treaties with cities, peoples, and other kingdoms. Service to these kings was understood in personal terms, as a tie to a person and not an impersonal polity: the king’s men were his “friends.”

Succession was largely dynastic and the apparatus of the state was a patrimony. The kings too could move from one kingdom to another, or opportunistically carve out new realms for themselves. Subjects understood the king to be acting primarily in his own interest, in many cases as an exploiter. Royal patronage had its advantages, but the king was at best expected to merely honor treaties and do his subjects some “favors” or be “well-disposed toward them,” not to work all night in order to benefit his people.
They were not “his people” to begin with. There was no concept of service to a
because there was no
no republic.

zh: 这些多族群王国除被国王权力维系外几乎无凝聚，通常除此外无集体身份。除或许马其顿的马其顿人外，不存在依身份、历史、法律地位、宗教与习俗统一所有臣民的政体观念。除埃及部分例外，行政、法律、税收与兵役一般不统一，且无论如何不被理解为一个人民的集体自治而是王权工具。各地也没有统一规范个人身份的法律：国王在其统治的许多城市中甚至常不是公民。因此其合法性不源于一个同意的政体，而源于继承、征服权（通常继承）、军事勇武与神性品质、恩宠或血统。
en: These multiethnic kingdoms had little coherence beyond being held together by the power of the king, and they usually had no collective identity beyond that. Excepting perhaps the Macedonians in Macedonia, there was no notion of a polity uniting all subjects in terms of identity, history, legal status, religion, and custom. With the partial exception of Egypt, administration, law, taxation, and military service were generally not uniform and, in any case, were understood not as the collective self-rule of a people but as the instruments of royal power. There was no uniform law of persons: the kings were often not even citizens in many of the cities that they ruled. Their legitimacy, therefore, was not derived from a consenting polity, but through inheritance, right of conquest (usually inherited), military prowess, and divine qualities, favor, or ancestry.

zh: 这完全不是拜占庭帝国呈现的图景，后者是罗马人的

构想为文化上希腊的，无论希腊文化形式多么服务于表达罗马观念。”甚至罗马希腊主义“也带有鲜明罗马道德论争的色彩，这在托勒密、阿塔罗斯和塞琉古诸王朝早期的希腊主义中找不到平行。”
皇帝的统治是一种服务形式，离开该功能不可想象。来自不同世纪与体裁的一系列文本确认这一点。我在此只引少数以展示该观念被皇帝与作者肯定或视为当然的强调，而这些人在其他事项尤其宗教上看法差异极大。但他们确有的共同点是罗马政体成员身份。四世纪初皇帝伽列里乌斯解释迫害基督徒意在“共和国之利与益（
/ τοῖς δημοσίοις）……依罗马人的古老法律与公共秩序。”
优西比乌在其
中同样视为当然：皇帝在和平时期的工作是“恢复
”——在此呼应奥古斯都恢复共和国——“促进各人利益，并为其所治理者的
之利安排法律。”
再次依被统治者定义；它不是“国家”。一世纪后尤纳皮奥斯——末代异教皇帝尤利安的辩护者——写道其英雄夺权“不是因为渴望王位……或追求庸俗民望，而是因为他知道这利于
当阿纳斯塔修斯一世491年被选为皇帝并在赛马场向人群致谢时，他确保承认“我并非不知道为全体之共同安全（κοινὴ σωτηρία）加于我的是多么大的责任重担”，并“我恳求全能的上帝，使你们发现我在公共事务（τὰ πράγματα）上如你们如今一致选我时（ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ κοινῇ ἐκλογῇ）所期望的那样努力。”
Theophanes Continuatus（十世纪中）致君士坦丁七世的序言说“皇帝须践行结合文学修养而益于
之事。”
en: This is not at all the picture presented by the Byzantine empire, which was the

of the Romans. Many scholars have defined Byzantium as an extension of Hellenistic civilization, a move that implicitly detaches it from the Roman tradition. However, in Byzantium as before, “the Romans never conceived of the

as culturally Greek, no matter how much Greek cultural forms served to express Roman ideas.” Even Roman Hellenism “was colored by distinctly Roman moral debates which find no parallels in the earlier dynastic Hellenism of Ptolemies, Attalids, or Seleucids.”

The emperor’s rule was a form of service and unthinkable apart from that function. A range of texts from different centuries and genres confirms this. I will cite only a few here to illustrate the emphasis with which the idea was affirmed, or taken for granted, by emperors and authors who differed greatly in their outlook on other matters, especially religion. But what they did have in common was membership in the Roman polity. In the early fourth century, the emperor Galerius explained that the persecution of the Christians was intended for “the advantage and benefit of the republic (
/ τοῖς δημοσίοις)... in accordance with the ancient laws and public order of the Romans.”
Eusebios likewise took it for granted in his
that the job of an emperor in peace was “to restore the
”—echoing here Augustus’s restoration of the republic—“to promote the interest of each person, and to arrange laws for the advantage of the
of those whom he governed.”
The

is again defined in terms of the ruled; it is not “the state.” A century later Eunapios, apologist of the last pagan emperor Julian, wrote that his hero seized power “not because he lusted after kingship... or sought vulgar popularity, but because he knew that this was to the advantage of the

When Anastasios I was elected emperor in 491 and was thanking the crowds in the hippodrome, he made sure to acknowledge, “I am not unaware how great a burden of responsibility has been placed upon me for the common safety (κοινὴ σωτηρία) of all,” and “I entreat God the Almighty that you will find me working as hard at public affairs (τὰ πράγματα) as you had hoped when you universally elected me now (ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ κοινῇ ἐκλογῇ).”
The preface of Theophanes Continuatus (mid-tenth century), addressed to Konstantinos VII, says that “an emperor is required to practice things that bring advantage to the
in combination with literary culture.”

zh: 皇帝应努力为臣民之益工作、这是其职位基本功能的观念，表达于多于此处能引的文本。事实上它是所有涉及
的叙事、讲话、宣告与文件的明示或底层假设。它是皇帝自己乐于承认且从不怀疑的东西。每位皇帝也努力确保其臣民知道他清楚理解这一点，仿佛是他们之间的一种“契约”，并说服他们他符合他们心中理想皇帝的形象。这套教条陈陈相因，本是要让臣民放下戒心，我们可不能也被它麻痹。我们后文将看到这一公关努力至关重要且不容失败，因为拜占庭舆论严厉而不宽容，失败可能给在位皇帝带来灾难。皇帝自己自愿相对于
定义其职位。我决定在此从法律、行政与战争领域给出一些代表性文本，尽管还有其他时刻与体裁可用来证明同一点。
en: The idea that the emperor was supposed to work hard for the benefit of his subjects, that this was the basic function of his position, is expressed in more texts than can be cited here. In fact, it is the explicit or underlying assumption of all narratives, speeches, pronouncements, and documents relating to the

It was something that the emperors themselves readily acknowledged and never doubted. Each emperor also tried hard to ensure that his subjects knew that he understood this clearly, as if it were a kind of “contract” between them, and to persuade them that he lived up to the image that they had of an ideal emperor. We must not, however, allow the banality and repetitious nature of this doctrine to lull us as it was meant to lull them. We will see later that this public relations effort was of critical importance and could not be allowed to fail, for Byzantine public opinion was harsh and unforgiving and the consequences of failure could be catastrophic for a reign. The emperors themselves willingly defined their position in relation to the
I have decided to present some representative texts here from the spheres of law, administration, and warfare, though there are other moments and genres that could be used to prove the same points.

总之皇帝表明其职位的主要目的是益于臣民，且这是证成其所颁一切立法的理由。
此外这些臣民不像我们学术中那样被想象为被武力震慑的随机族群聚合，而是如西塞罗所定义，一个具有须保存的自然秩序的统一人民的政体。在其法律汇编

In sum, emperors made it clear that the main purpose of their office was to benefit their subjects, and that this was the reason that justified all the legislation they issued.

These subjects, moreover, were not imagined, as in our scholarship, to be an agglomeration of random ethnicities cowed by force, but, as Cicero had defined it, a polity of a unified people with a natural order that had to be preserved. In the preface to his codification of the laws, the

这一般是对所有皇帝的期望，他们接受它为工作的一部分。
但修辞不限于他们：同样的似乎也被期望于所有帝国职能官员，尽管出于明显原因他们在存世文献中出现较少。但每当其中之一转而写自己这类人时，我们再次发现通宵苦干的修辞。
在此意义上皇帝只是共和国更尊贵的职能官员。
en: Turning to administration, the message was that some emperors never slept, so hard did they labor on their subjects’ behalf. The idea was a trope of the imperial idea and was broadcast in legal prefaces, especially by Justinian, who even described himself in a public inscription as “the Sleepless Emperor.” Prokopios tried to turn this around to make him appear sinister, but it was a banal image.
Later emperors who did not sleep included Leon III (on behalf of
), Basileios I (on behalf of his subjects and
), and Nikephoros III Botaneiates (over

Psellos wrote of Isaakios I that “his eye is sleepless and not one of you has seen him indulging in any pleasure during the entire length of his reign, or feasting extravagantly, or celebrating conspicuously, or taking any rest in sleep, or sparing his body in his labors.”
This was generally expected of all emperors, and they accepted it as part of the job.

But the rhetoric was not confined to them: the same seems to have been expected of all imperial functionaries, though they appear less frequently in the surviving literature, for obvious reasons. But whenever one of them turned to write about his own kind, we find again the rhetoric of working hard through the night.
The emperor was, in this sense, only a more exalted functionary of the republic.

zh: 战争是另一个可为政体劳作的领域。希拉克略“为其
冒生命之险。”
亲征的皇帝确保其臣民知道他们为谁而战、承担个人危险。在其墓志铭中巴西尔二世自夸“我一生保持警醒，守护新罗马的孩子们。”
Psellos 赞伊萨克为“罗马人的大益”，他“愿死一万次以增大罗马帝国。”
同一作者似是而非地论证那位最不擅军旅的皇帝君士坦丁九世·莫诺马科斯的家族名“指定了那为国家（κράτος）预先且独自面对危险者，一个超越所有人的卓越战士，为我们人民的共同荣耀（ὑπὲρ τῆς κοινῆς τοῦ γένους εὐκλείας）单挑作战。”
还可引更多例子，但让我们考虑罗曼努斯四世的悲剧一例。在一篇

Emperors, given their extraordinary powers, were naturally held to the highest standard. They in turn evaluated their subjects’ contributions. 十三世纪初一个喜剧轶事醒目地揭示臣民对皇帝的期望与皇帝希望被如何看待。它属于帝国形象的一个亚体裁，即与平民的相遇以展示皇帝对其问题的个人关心。这些小品凸显帝国美德从而为臣民感知定调。某个傻子四处说很快会有一位好皇帝。这话传到皇帝塞奥多罗斯·拉斯卡里斯耳中，他叫人把那人带来。
en: It was by the same standard that the emperors themselves were evaluated by their subjects, both during and after their reigns. Opinions differed about the particulars of each case, but there was consensus about the standard. This did not change in the later period.

A comic anecdote from the early thirteenth century strikingly reveals what subjects expected from their emperors and how emperors wanted to be perceived. It belongs to a subgenre of imperial imagery, namely, the encounter with a common person that showcases an emperor’s personal interest in his problems. These vignettes highlighted imperial virtues and so set the tone for subjects’ perceptions. A certain simpleton was going around saying that soon there would be a good emperor. This came to the ears of the emperor, Theodoros Laskaris, and he had the man brought to him.

zh: “那我是什么？”他说。“在你看来我不像好皇帝吗？”

en: “The sun shines and so heats us and gives us light, but we are not thankful to it. It fulfills the function that has been set for it. And you are doing what you ought to do, toiling and laboring, as you say, on behalf of your compatriots.”

en: “So... if I give you some gifts, will I be good then?” “Yes, of course.” And so he gave him clothes and money.

en: Prokopios also considered emperors to be basically magistrates. At one point, in criticizing Justinian’s extraordinary rituals of submission, he refers to a time when the emperor could be ranked “among the rest of the magistrates.”
Psellos was not reacting against excessive pomp but only to incompetence when he declared that Konstantinos IX did not understand “the nature of the
that is a form of service to benefit one’s subjects (λειτουργία τίς ἐστι λυσιτελὴς εἰς τὸ ὑπήκοον) and it requires alertness of mind to properly administrate political affairs.”
This is the view of the office that Psellos maintains throughout his history and the standard by which he judges all emperors.
Many Palaiologan texts also reflect the assumption that emperors were basically executive officials who wielded power that had been delegated to them by the republic.

en: One might suppose, with Magdalino, that all these writers were classically educated and therefore out of touch with Byzantine realities. But this postulates unnecessary polarities and conflates their education, which was Greek and theoretical, with the ideology of the polity, which was Roman and built into political practice. The emperors themselves, as we have seen repeatedly, defined their own position within a republican framework—“I rule for your benefit, not mine.” A theoretical education merely enabled the likes of Psellos to articulate precisely this republican aspect of the Byzantine polity and make it the basis for a critique and reform. that is, at the head of a section devoted to civil ceremonies—as opposed to religious ceremonies—and the promotions of dignitaries. The emperor and the Augusta were thus placed at the top of a hierarchy which descended to the level of the office head and
